lba_qa.q: A square garden has an area of 144 square metres. Find the length of one side.
lba_qa.a:
Area of a square = side x side = side^2.

Side = square root of 144
= 12

So each side of the garden is 12 metres. ✅

lba_qa.q: A gardener wants to plant 256 saplings in a square arrangement (equal rows and columns). How many saplings will be in each row?
lba_qa.a:
Number in each row = square root of total saplings.
= square root of 256
= 16

So there will be 16 saplings in each row. ✅

lba_qa.q: Find the smallest number by which 72 must be multiplied to make it a perfect square.
lba_qa.a:
Prime factorise 72:
72 = 2 x 2 x 2 x 3 x 3
= (2 x 2) x (3 x 3) x 2

The lone factor is 2. Multiply by 2 to pair it.
72 x 2 = 144 = 12^2.

So the smallest number is 2. ✅

lba_qa.q: A square hall has area 625 square metres. A tile is to be placed along one side. Find the side length.
lba_qa.a:
Side = square root of area
= square root of 625
= 25

So each side of the hall is 25 metres. ✅

lba_qa.q: Find the square root of 1024 by prime factorisation.
lba_qa.a:
1024 = 2^10 (ten 2's).

Pair them: (2x2)(2x2)(2x2)(2x2)(2x2)
Take one 2 from each pair: 2 x 2 x 2 x 2 x 2 = 32.

So the square root of 1024 is 32. ✅

lba_qa.q: A number ends in the digit 5 and is a perfect square. What digit will be in the units place of its square root?
lba_qa.a:
A perfect square ending in 5 has its square root also ending in 5 (since 5 x 5 = 25).

For example, 225 = 15^2 and 625 = 25^2.

So the units digit of the square root is 5. ✅

lba_qa.q: Find the smallest number that must be subtracted from 130 to make it a perfect square.
lba_qa.a:
The perfect square just below 130 is 121 = 11^2.
(The next, 144 = 12^2, is above 130.)

130 - 121 = 9

So 9 must be subtracted to get 121. ✅

lba_qa.q: A square sheet has area 81 square cm. Find its perimeter.
lba_qa.a:
Side = square root of 81 = 9 cm.

Perimeter = 4 x side
= 4 x 9
= 36 cm

So the perimeter is 36 cm. ✅

lba_qa.q: How many students can stand in a perfect square formation from a group of 200, and how many are left out?
lba_qa.a:
The perfect square just below 200 is 196 = 14^2.

Students in the square = 196 (14 rows of 14).
Left out = 200 - 196 = 4.

So 196 students form the square and 4 are left out. ✅

lba_qa.q: Find the square of 25 using the pattern that a number ending in 5 squared ends in 25.
lba_qa.a:
For a number ending in 5, square = (first digit) x (first digit + 1) followed by 25.
Here first digit = 2.
2 x (2 + 1) = 2 x 3 = 6.

So 25^2 = 625. ✅
